symbols.name: kappa
symbols.role: observable lower separation for total positive-layer stayer mass

symbols.name: Dpot
symbols.role: protocol-assigned tiers under both assignments; the control protocol retains baseline placement, while the treatment algorithm may retain or upgrade the assigned tier but is prohibited from downgrading it

symbols.name: Mclass

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: \(W=(Z,D,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\) is defined by the observation/coarsening map: \(D=D_Z\), \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_{Z,D_Z}\) if \(D_Z>0\), and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=\star\) if \(D_Z=0\). These equalities are conventions of the map, not restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_L\).

symbols.name: Dclass
symbols.role: compatible observable laws with separated stayer denominator

symbols.name: mu

symbols.name: v

symbols.name: phi

symbols.name: Hlo

symbols.name: Hup

symbols.name: muhat

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: \(G\) has independent arm blocks with covariance \(\{\operatorname{diag}(\mu_z)-\mu_z\mu_z^{\top}\}/e\) for \(z=1\) and denominator \(1-e\) for \(z=0\)

novel.justification: This is a researcher-imposed cross-world protocol restriction. It is credible when control retains a participant's baseline assigned tier and a treatment assignment algorithm is mechanically permitted only to retain or upgrade that tier, never to downgrade it. It is not supported by Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal: their Assumption 2 is only binary positive-selection monotonicity and permits movements in either direction among positive layers.

This is a maintained observable positive-denominator and inference-stability restriction, not a consequence attributed to a published one-stratum condition. It is directly checkable from the two arm tier margins and is satisfied whenever margins compatible with strong tier monotonicity force at least \(\kappa\) mass to remain in positive tiers, as in the explicit two-layer witness.

definitions.name: Strongly monotone protocol-tier full-data class \(\mathcal M_L\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_L=\{P^{\star}: P^{\star}\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass{:}random\mbox{-}assignment}\text{ and }\mathrm{ass{:}strong\mbox{-}tier\mbox{-}monotonicity}\text{ for the fixed }L\}\)

definitions.name: Separated compatible observable class \(\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}=\{P:\exists P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_L\text{ inducing }P\text{ and }\mu(P)\in\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\}\)

definitions.name: Observable arm-cell compatibility set \(\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\)
definitions.construction: For \(v=(v_0,v_1)\in\Delta^{2L}\times\Delta^{2L}\), set \(r_0(v)=v_{0,0^{\star}}\), \(r_d(v)=v_{0,(d,0)}+v_{0,(d,1)}\), \(c_0(v)=v_{1,0^{\star}}\), \(c_d(v)=v_{1,(d,0)}+v_{1,(d,1)}\), \(q_{0d}(v)=v_{0,(d,1)}\), \(q_{1d}(v)=v_{1,(d,1)}\), \(R_d(v)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}r_j(v)\), \(C_d(v)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}c_j(v)\), and \(\ell_d(v)=\max\{0,C_d(v)-R_{d-1}(v)\}\). Then \(\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}=\{v\in\Delta^{2L}\times\Delta^{2L}:C_d(v)\le R_d(v)\text{ for }d=0,\ldots,L-1,\ \sum_{d=1}^{L}\ell_d(v)\ge\kappa\}\). The cumulative inequalities are the observable necessary-and-sufficient compatibility conditions for an upper-triangular layer coupling; the simplex coordinates already impose \(0\le q_{0d}(v)\le r_d(v)\) and \(0\le q_{1d}(v)\le c_d(v)\).

definitions.name: Closed-form endpoint construction
definitions.construction: \(s_d^-=\min\{u_d,\max\{\ell_d,a_d\}\}\), \(s_d^+=\max\{\ell_d,b_d\}\), \(A_-=\sum_{d=1}^{L}(\ell_d-a_d)_+\), \(B_-=\sum_{d=1}^{L}s_d^-\), \(A_+=\sum_{d=1}^{L}b_d\), and \(B_+=\sum_{d=1}^{L}s_d^+\). The closed-form endpoint pair associated with these primitives is \((A_-/B_-,A_+/B_+)\).

definitions.name: Expanded-state transport network
definitions.construction: Use arm states \(\mathcal E=\{0^{\star}\}\cup\{(d,y):d=1,\ldots,L,\ y\in\{0,1\}\}\), connect a left state at layer \(i\) to a right state at layer \(j\) exactly when \(i\le j\), assign the observed arm-cell probabilities as margins, and label a diagonal arc by stayer cost \(\sigma=1\) and by harm cost \(\eta=1\) exactly for \((d,1)\to(d,0)\)

definitions.name: Nondegenerate two-layer observable and response-law witness
Ambient endpoint extension \(\phi\)
definitions.construction: For a generic arm-cell vector \(v\), decode \(r(v),c(v),q_0(v),q_1(v)\) as in \(\mathrm{def{:}observable\mbox{-}mu\mbox{-}domain}\), form \(R(v),C(v),\ell(v),u(v),a(v),b(v)\), and evaluate \(B_-(v)=\sum_{d=1}^{L}\min\{u_d(v),\max\{\ell_d(v),a_d(v)\}\}\) and \(B_+(v)=\sum_{d=1}^{L}\max\{\ell_d(v),b_d(v)\}\). On \(\mathcal U=\{v:B_-(v)>\kappa/2,\ B_+(v)>\kappa/2\}\), define \[\phi(v)=\left(\frac{\sum_{d=1}^{L}(\ell_d(v)-a_d(v))_+}{B_-(v)},\frac{\sum_{d=1}^{L}b_d(v)}{B_+(v)}\right).\] Set \(\phi(v)=(0,1)\) outside \(\mathcal U\). For every \(v\in\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\), define the common-domain endpoint functionals by \(H_-(v)=\pi_1\phi(v)\) and \(H_+(v)=\pi_2\phi(v)\).

definitions.name: Hong--Li numerical-delta implementation
definitions.construction: For fixed \(L\), after verifying Hadamard directional differentiability of the ambient map \(\phi\) at the observable law and conditional consistency of the multinomial bootstrap direction, compute \(T_n^{\star}=\{\phi(\widehat\mu_n+\varepsilon_nG_n^{\star})-\phi(\widehat\mu_n)\}/\varepsilon_n\), where \(\varepsilon_n\downarrow0\) and \(\sqrt n\,\varepsilon_n\to\infty\), and apply the pointwise numerical-delta theorem of Hong--Li. This is a direct implementation of their theorem, including at hinge ties and structural-zero cells once its tangent-space and bootstrap premises are checked, and is not a novel inferential claim.

definitions.name: Confidence-set image construction
definitions.construction: Given a simultaneous \((1-\alpha)\)-confidence region \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) for \(\mu\), set \(J_{n,\alpha}=[\inf_{v\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}}\pi_1\phi(v),\ \sup_{v\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}}\pi_2\phi(v)]\) when the intersection is nonempty and set \(J_{n,\alpha}=[0,1]\) otherwise. Equivalently, the extrema are over \(H_-(v)=\pi_1\phi(v)\) and \(H_+(v)=\pi_2\phi(v)\), both defined on \(\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\). The known implementation-level containment \(v\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\Rightarrow[H_-(v),H_+(v)]\subseteq J_{n,\alpha}\) is merely the image-of-a-covered-set observation and carries no separate proof obligation or novelty claim.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\), the projection of \(\Theta(P)\) onto \((p_{11},\ldots,p_{LL})\) is exactly \(\prod_{d=1}^{L}[\ell_d,u_d]\). Every vector in this box admits an upper-triangular nonnegative completion with row margins \(r\) and column margins \(c\), including when observable cells are zero.
statements.justification: The box projection is the structural cancellation that removes the high-dimensional response-type optimizer.
statements.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds, but it does not state the simultaneous Cartesian projection of all positive-layer diagonal response-type masses.
statements.consumer: Software for protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiments can replace response-table enumeration by \(2L\) observable diagonal endpoints.

statements.statement: The expanded-state transport network has \(2L^2+4L+1\) admissible arcs, and its feasible couplings are in bijection with realized-arm joint distributions induced by laws in \(\mathcal M_L\). The decoder preserves \((s,h)\); unused potential outcomes may be completed arbitrarily.
statements.justification: The decoder supplies an independent finite-dimensional sharpness certificate and a destructive check on missing-outcome handling.
statements.gap: Generic transportation representations do not identify which network coordinates equal same-layer harm under multilayer missingness.
statements.consumer: Auditors of bounds software for protocol-controlled tier assignments obtain a latent-cell program against which the closed form can be tested.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\), the set of all \((s,h)\) induced by full-data laws \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_L\) that agree with \(P\) is exactly \(\mathcal K(P)\). In particular, all layerwise stayer and harm coordinates satisfying the displayed hinge inequalities are jointly attainable by one normalized full-data law.
statements.justification: Coordinatewise bounds are insufficient for an aggregate ratio unless a single law attains every chosen coordinate simultaneously.
statements.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds. De Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele give sharp multi-tier benefit and harm bounds when the tiers are categories of the outcome itself. Possebom--Riva and Kallus characterize binary harm couplings. None of these results allocates selectively observed units across latent same-layer stayers or gives the exact cross-world stayer--harm prism for protocol-assigned selection tiers.
statements.consumer: A protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiment can report harm among participants whose assigned tier would be unchanged under either assignment.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\) with arm-cell vector \(\mu\), the sharp identified set for \(H\) is \([H_-(\mu),H_+(\mu)]\), where \(H_-(\mu)=\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}(\ell_d-a_d)_+\}/\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}\min(u_d,\max(\ell_d,a_d))\}\) and \(H_+(\mu)=\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}b_d\}/\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}\max(\ell_d,b_d)\}\). Both endpoints and every interior value are attainable, and the endpoints require \(O(L)\) arithmetic operations.
statements.justification: A closed form makes the unidentified-denominator target usable for comparative statics, diagnostics, and inference.
statements.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds, and de Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele give sharp benefit and harm bounds across ordered outcome categories. The distinct object here is harm within latent same-layer stayers under selectively observed protocol-assigned selection tiers: both its numerator and denominator are unidentified, and its sharp ratio endpoints arise by contraction of the joint prism.
statements.consumer: Bounds software for protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiments can compute sharp multilayer harm endpoints in time linear in the number of layers.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\) with arm-cell vector \(\mu\), \(H_-(\mu)>0\) if and only if there exists \(d\in\{1,\ldots,L\}\) such that \(q_{0d}-q_{1d}>R_d-C_d\).
statements.justification: The iff inequality turns a latent cross-world conclusion into an observable sorting-capacity certificate.
statements.gap: Published probability-of-causation bounds and harm bounds across observed outcome categories, including de Aguas--Krumscheid--Pensar--Biele, do not provide a necessary-and-sufficient sorting-capacity condition for harm within latent stayers at protocol-assigned selection tiers.
statements.consumer: An applied researcher can diagnose unavoidable harm layer by layer without solving a latent allocation problem.

statements.statement: The table \(v^{\mathrm{ex}}\) has strictly positive observed success and failure cells at both positive layers and belongs to \(\mathcal V_{2,49/100}\). Its observable quantities are \(\ell=(1/4,1/4)\), \(u=(7/20,1/4)\), \(a=(3/20,19/100)\), and \(b=(3/10,1/5)\), so its joint prism is \[\{(s_1,h_1):1/4\le s_1\le7/20,\ (s_1-3/20)_+\le h_1\le\min\{s_1,3/10\}\}\times\{(s_2,h_2):s_2=1/4,\ 3/50\le h_2\le1/5\}.\] The endpoint composition gives \(\phi(v^{\mathrm{ex}})=(8/25,10/11)\). Moreover, \(q_{01}-q_{11}=1/5>1/10=R_1-C_1\) and \(q_{02}-q_{12}=3/50>0=R_2-C_2\), so the unavoidable-harm certificate holds. The couplings \(\Gamma^-\) and \(\Gamma^+\) have the displayed observable margins and respectively yield \((s,h)=((1/4,1/4),(1/10,3/50))\) and \((s,h)=((3/10,1/4),(3/10,1/5))\); decoding them produces full-data response laws attaining the lower and upper endpoints.
statements.justification: The exact rational witness checks the prism, the interior-hinge upper optimizer, the observable certificate, and both response-law attainments in one nondegenerate design.
statements.gap: The closest papers do not provide an all-layer response-law table that attains both endpoints of a ratio with an unidentified same-layer denominator.
statements.consumer: The table is a regression fixture for bounds software restricted to protocol-controlled tier assignments and a reproducible audit target for the constructive proof.

sampling_model.design: Independent Bernoulli assignment of a protocol-controlled tier-upgrade algorithm with \(P(Z=1)=e\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.units: An independent and identically distributed sample of participants \(W_1,\ldots,W_n\) whose conditional arm-cell vector \(\mu\) lies in the explicit observable compatibility set \(\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary randomized assignment \(Z\) in a protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiment. Control retains baseline placement; the treatment algorithm may retain or upgrade a participant's assigned tier and is prohibited from downgrading it. Thus \(D_z\) records assigned tier rather than unrestricted voluntary firm choice. The cross-world condition \(P^{\star}(D_1\ge D_0)=1\) is researcher-imposed, maintained, and neither validated nor point-identified by the observed arm margins.
sampling_model.overlap: The assignment probability satisfies \(0<e<1\). The maintained observable positive-denominator and inference-stability restriction is \(\sum_{d=1}^{L}\ell_d\ge\kappa>0\); it is not attributed to a one-stratum positive-mass theorem.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The primitive is the finite vector of empirical arm-state probabilities \(\widehat\mu_n\); no smoothing or learned nuisance is required.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1(iii) gives sharp closed-form bounds for the weighted aggregate local controlled direct effect under multilayer sample selection.

Accessible arXiv v6 Proposition 2 gives sharp conditional probability-of-causation bounds for the always-observed subgroup under conditional random assignment, positive mass, and monotone binary sample selection; journal proposition identity was not independently verified.
Theorem 2 gives a closed sharp interval for the fraction negatively affected using Fr\'echet bounds on observed treatment-arm marginals.

Proposition 5 and equations (7)--(8) give sharp Fr\'echet bounds for benefit across ordered outcome categories without outcome monotonicity, with tiered harm obtained by reversing the ordered-category comparison.
The directional delta method applies to Hadamard directionally differentiable maps, and valid resampling estimates the directional derivative rather than bootstrapping a nonlinear map naively.
A shrinking finite-difference evaluation consistently estimates the law of a directionally differentiable transform pointwise.
Calibrated projection delivers confidence intervals for projections of partially identified parameters with uniform asymptotic validity.
Aggregated conditional linear-program support values are regular under a margin condition and admit root-\(n\) Gaussian inference.

tldr: Random assignment identifies the two arm-specific tier--outcome margins but not which participants retain the same positive assigned tier or which such participants are harmed. Here the layers are selectively observed, protocol-assigned selection tiers, not categories of the outcome. The maintained restriction \(P^{\star}(D_1\ge D_0)=1\) is researcher-imposed strong monotonicity for a protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiment: control retains baseline placement, whereas the treatment algorithm may retain or upgrade an assigned tier but cannot downgrade it. It is distinct from ordinary Lee or binary positive-selection monotonicity and is neither validated nor point-identified from observed arm margins. Under this restriction, the entire feasible diagonal of the response-type table is a Cartesian box, and binary potential-outcome completion converts each diagonal coordinate into an independent hinge region for harm. This exact cross-world stayer--harm prism yields sharp \(O(L)\) endpoints for a ratio with unidentified numerator and denominator and an observable iff certificate for unavoidable harm; an exact nondegenerate two-layer response table attains \([8/25,10/11]\). Fixed-\(L\) pointwise numerical-delta calculations and confidence-set image projection are implementation devices inherited from general results, not research contributions.

project_justification.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already supplies sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds under multilayer selection. Their Assumption 2 imposes only binary positive-selection monotonicity and permits both directions among positive layers, so it neither states nor supports ordered-layer monotonicity. De Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele provide the closest multi-tier harm comparison: their sharp bounds concern movement across tiers of ordered outcome categories. Binary harm results handle one observed stratum or fully observed arm marginals. No inspected result characterizes harm within latent same-layer stayers jointly with an unidentified sum of same-tier stayer masses under selectively observed protocol-assigned selection tiers.
project_justification.niche: In a protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiment, a researcher may maintain strong monotonicity because control retains baseline placement and the treatment assignment algorithm is prohibited from downgrading tiers. This cross-world restriction is stronger than ordinary Lee or binary positive-selection monotonicity and is not learned from the observed arm margins; conditional on it, upper-triangular support makes residual response-type transport strict triangular.
project_justification.fill: Three identification theorems establish the diagonal box, the exact joint stayer--harm prism, and sharp \(O(L)\) endpoints for protocol-assigned tiers. The unavoidable-harm corollary and exact rational two-layer attainment witness make the identification result directly auditable. Generic numerical-delta and confidence-set image operations remain ordinary implementation prose.

related_work: Kroft, Mourifi\'e, and Vayalinkal study multilayer sample selection, and their Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds. Their Assumption 2 is only binary positive-selection monotonicity: treatment cannot turn positive selection into nonselection, but movements in both directions among positive layers remain admissible. It therefore provides no precedent or support for the ordered-layer condition \(P^{\star}(D_1\ge D_0)=1\). That condition is imposed solely by this paper as a cross-world protocol restriction for a tier-upgrade experiment in which control retains baseline placement and the treatment assignment algorithm cannot downgrade an assigned tier. It is stronger than ordinary Lee or binary positive-selection monotonicity, and observed arm margins neither validate nor point-identify it. The contribution conditional on that restriction is the exact cross-world binary stayer--harm prism and the closed-form contraction of a ratio whose harm numerator and same-tier-stayer denominator are both unidentified. No applicability claim is made for settings in which tiers arise from unrestricted voluntary firm choice. The accessible arXiv v6 of Possebom and Riva derives sharp probability-of-causation bounds in one always-observed binary-selection stratum under conditional random assignment, positive mass, and monotone sample selection. As an explicitly non-novel boundary check, when all positive-layer mass is concentrated at one layer \(d^{\star}\), the present interval is \([\max\{0,q_{0d^{\star}}-q_{1d^{\star}}\}/r_{d^{\star}},\ \min\{q_{0d^{\star}},c_{d^{\star}}-q_{1d^{\star}}\}/r_{d^{\star}}]\). For \(q_{0d^{\star}}>0\), this formula follows by outcome complementation and identified-mass rescaling of Possebom--Riva, accessible arXiv:2210.01938v6, Proposition 2, using the factor \(q_{0d^{\star}}/r_{d^{\star}}\); for \(q_{0d^{\star}}=0\), both endpoints are zero directly. This cited specialization is not a research result or solve target. The journal article text was inaccessible during verification, so no claim is made that its proposition numbering or displayed formula is identical to arXiv v6. The maintained observable restriction \(\sum_d\ell_d\ge\kappa\) is imposed as a positive-denominator and inference-stability condition and is not attributed to Possebom--Riva's one-stratum positive-mass condition. De Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele provide the closer multi-tier harm comparator. Their Proposition 5 and equations (7)--(8) give sharp Fr\'echet bounds for benefit across tiers of ordered outcome categories without outcome monotonicity, and their tiered-harm analysis reverses that outcome-category comparison. Those outcome tiers are not the selectively observed protocol-assigned selection tiers \(D_z\) studied here. Their result neither supplies the ordered-selection diagonal box nor subsumes the joint region for latent same-layer stayer and harm masses or the resulting unidentified-denominator ratio endpoints. Kallus derives sharp fraction-harmed bounds from observed treatment-arm outcome marginals; his binary coupling informs completion within a fixed diagonal tier, not upper-triangular tier transport. Fang and Santos provide directional-delta calculus, and Hong and Li provide the pointwise numerical-delta theorem. For fixed \(L\), using the latter is a direct application after verifying the ambient directional derivative and conditional multinomial bootstrap premises, including the relevant boundary tangent space; no new inference theorem is claimed. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye provide substantive projection inference for partially identified parameters, while mapping a covered observable confidence set through \(H_-\) and \(H_+\) on \(\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\) is only the known image-of-a-covered-set fallback. Khandamiryan and Semenova study regular inference for aggregated conditional linear programs; that work is adjacent to, but not a comparator target for, the fixed finite-cell identification claims here.
technical_internal_limitation: The observable floor \(\sum_d\ell_d\ge\kappa\) is a maintained positive-denominator and inference-stability restriction, not a theorem inherited from a binary always-observed stratum. The researcher-imposed condition \(P^{\star}(D_1\ge D_0)=1\) is a separate, load-bearing cross-world restriction on protocol-assigned tiers. Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Assumption 2 is only binary positive-selection monotonicity and permits both directions among positive layers, so it provides no support for this ordered-layer restriction. The restriction is stronger than ordinary Lee or binary positive-selection monotonicity, is not validated or point-identified from observed arm margins, and is not credible for unrestricted voluntary firm choice without an enforcing assignment protocol. Reciprocal transitions between positive tiers can couple diagonal coordinates and destroy the box. For fixed \(L\), pointwise numerical-delta inference follows directly from Hong--Li after the ambient endpoint map's directional derivative and the conditional multinomial bootstrap premises are verified at the observable law, including structural-zero tangent directions; this implementation step carries no novelty claim and does not imply uniform validity along local sequences crossing a tie. The image of a simultaneous confidence region over \(\mathcal V_{L,\kappa}\) is a known definition-level fallback, and its containment is not a research result. No growing-\(L\), covariate-assisted, efficiency, uniform-inference, regime-comparison, or empirical reanalysis claim is part of this core.
honest_scope: The research contribution is identification conditional on researcher-imposed strong monotonicity of protocol-assigned selection tiers: the diagonal box, exact joint binary stayer--harm prism, sharp closed-form ratio contraction, and iff harm certificate. These tiers index selectively observed assignments rather than the ordered outcome categories in de Aguas--Krumscheid--Pensar--Biele. A credible motivating design is a protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiment in which control retains baseline placement and the treatment algorithm may retain or upgrade but cannot downgrade the assigned tier. The restriction is maintained rather than inferred: it is distinct from ordinary Lee or binary positive-selection monotonicity and is neither validated nor point-identified by observed arm margins. Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Assumption 2 permits both directions among positive layers and supplies no precedent or support for the ordering. The exact \(L=2\) arm-cell and response-law tables certify a nondegenerate attainable instance with bounds \([8/25,10/11]\), and the network decoder is supporting. The observable \(\kappa\)-floor is maintained for a uniformly positive target denominator and inferential stability rather than claimed as a published implication. Confidence-set image containment is retained only inside the implementation definition as a known fallback. Fixed-\(L\) pointwise numerical-delta inference is a direct Hong--Li application once the ambient directional derivative and conditional multinomial bootstrap premises are verified, with no novelty or separate theorem claim. The one-positive-layer formula is only a non-novel boundary check: for \(q_{0d^{\star}}>0\), it is the outcome-complemented arXiv:2210.01938v6 Possebom--Riva Proposition 2 interval rescaled by \(q_{0d^{\star}}/r_{d^{\star}}\), and the zero-mass case is immediate. It is not a formal solve target or contribution; journal proposition identity was not independently verified.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorem 1, Sections 4.1--4.3, proof appendix, and Conclusion
seed_details.opportunity: Under researcher-imposed strong monotonicity of protocol-assigned tiers, characterize the joint projection of the upper-triangular response-type table onto positive diagonal masses and binary harm cells, then contract the resulting ratio without a generic linear program.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the paper's optimization of within-layer conditional means over dependent mixture weights by a simultaneous projection of every diagonal response-type mass together with its \(2\times2\) potential-outcome coupling.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining multilayer sample selection with fraction harmed, probability of causation, positive-layer stayers, and closed-form ratio bounds located the component literatures, including de Aguas--Krumscheid--Pensar--Biele on benefit and harm across ordered outcome categories, but no all-layer joint region for latent stayers across selectively observed selection tiers.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal because Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds.
seed_details.rebuttal: Theorem 1(iii) settles a weighted aggregate LCDE, while Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Assumption 2 imposes only binary positive-selection monotonicity and permits movements in both directions among positive layers. De Aguas--Krumscheid--Pensar--Biele settle sharp benefit and harm bounds across ordered outcome categories, not latent stayer strata induced by selective observation. Conditional on this paper's researcher-imposed strong monotonicity of protocol-assigned selection tiers, the proposed theorem instead characterizes cross-world binary harm cells jointly with every unknown same-tier mass and contracts the resulting ratio with unidentified numerator and denominator.

threads: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds. Their Assumption 2 is only binary positive-selection monotonicity and permits movements in both directions among positive layers; it does not provide precedent or support for ordered-layer monotonicity. The condition \(P^{\star}(D_1\ge D_0)=1\) is instead maintained solely as this paper's researcher-imposed protocol restriction and is not inferred from arm margins.

The accessible arXiv:2210.01938v6 of Possebom--Riva gives a constructive sharp probability-of-causation interval for one always-observed stratum under conditional random assignment, positive mass, and binary monotone selection; its Proposition 2 formula supplies the outcome-complemented and identified-mass-rescaled one-positive-layer boundary check. That specialization is non-novel and is not a solve target, while the cited construction does not address the multilayer joint region.

Kallus gives conditional Fr\'echet bounds for the fraction negatively affected when both arm marginals are observed; this supplies the within-diagonal \(2\times2\) completion but no selective-observation allocation.

De Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele Proposition 5 and equations (7)--(8) give sharp multi-tier benefit bounds without outcome monotonicity, and the paper treats harm by reversing movement across ordered outcome categories. This is the closer multi-tier harm comparator, but its tiers index categories of the outcome rather than selectively observed protocol-assigned selection tiers; it therefore supplies neither the ordered-selection diagonal box nor the joint same-layer stayer--harm prism or its ratio contraction.

Generic finite transportation and optimal-transport bounds supply computational representations, but the proposed strict-triangular cancellation yields the stronger Cartesian box and \(O(L)\) contraction.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The sharp outcome-category bounds of de Aguas--Krumscheid--Pensar--Biele do not subsume selective-observation response types. No inspected theorem gives the joint region \(\prod_{d=1}^{L}\{(s_d,h_d):\ell_d\le s_d\le u_d,\ (s_d-a_d)_+\le h_d\le\min(s_d,b_d)\}\), the corresponding closed-form ratio endpoints, or the cumulative sorting-capacity certificate.

threads: Fang--Santos give the directional delta method and explain ordinary-bootstrap failure without full differentiability.
Hong--Li give pointwise numerical-delta validity for Hadamard directionally differentiable maps.
For fixed \(L\), the endpoint calculation uses Hong--Li directly after checking the ambient derivative and conditional multinomial bootstrap premises, including structural-zero tangent directions.
literature_map.subsumption_check: No novelty gap is asserted: the numerical-delta calculation is implementation of published general theory, not a proposal statement or open question.

threads: Semenova conditions Lee monotonicity on covariates and builds orthogonal inference for mean bounds.
Kallus uses covariates to tighten harm bounds when outcomes are observed under both treatments.
Khandamiryan--Semenova average conditional linear-program values and derive an influence function under a margin condition.
Ji--Lei--Spector use optimal-transport duality to obtain model-agnostic covariate-assisted causal bounds, trading sharpness for robustness.
literature_map.subsumption_check: None of the inspected results establishes that optimizing conditional numerator--denominator support sets and then integrating yields sharp population endpoints for same-layer stayers.
